- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and forecast is significantly below recent history, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent history, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction to bearish signals.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 3–5% to correct for overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 10% of the 18-day history mean, apply a mean reversion bias toward the 18-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from high to low), delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature correction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing the 30-day curve with a 7-day moving average.
